item.title: Planning for Severe Winter Storms
item.description: Belvedere is preparing for a challenging winter, as a strong El Niño develops in the Pacific Ocean. Although the timing and severity of individual storms remain uncertain, the combination of heavy rainfall, elevated bay water levels, and seasonal king tides likely will increase the risk of flooding and other storm-related impacts across the community. Winter...

item.title: What the City Is Doing
item.description: The City's primary responsibilities during severe weather are protecting public safety, maintaining essential public infrastructure, and keeping our roads accessible for emergency responders. Belvedere’s Public Works crews are busy cleaning storm drains and catch basins, flushing drainage lines, clearing known flood-prone locations, and checking emergency pumps and generators. These measures are intended to improve drainage performance...

item.description: Timely and reliable information is essential during significant weather events. Residents are invited to attend a Get Ready for Super El Niño preparedness presentation at the Belvedere-Tiburon Library on either October 27 at 6pm or on November 4 at 11am. item.title: During a Storm
item.description: Avoid walking or driving through flooded areas. Floodwater can conceal hazards, and even shallow moving water can be dangerous. Never drive around road closures or barricades. Report fallen trees, blocked drainage facilities, or other non-emergency storm-related problems, contact the Belvedere Police Department at 415-435-3266. Report downed power lines to 911 and PG&E at 800-743-5002. Always...

item.title: Winter Storm Preparedness
item.description: A strong El Niño has formed in the Pacific, and forecasters expect it to be one of the most powerful on record. For Belvedere, that likely means intense, moisture-heavy storms, higher-than-normal tides, and a greater chance of flooding in low-lying areas, especially when storms arrive during winter king tides. item.title: Mallard Point Update
item.description: The City issued the bulkhead replacement permit on October 1, 2026, based on the developer satisfying all prerequisite conditions of approval and technical engineering reviews. Initial site work has begun, starting with security fencing, utility shutoffs, and completed fire department training exercises. item.description: Do you know a resident who has made a significant contribution to the community—someone who has volunteered their time and skills to help make Belvedere the wonderful place that it is? We want to honor that person! The nomination process is now open for the Citizen of the Year and the Citizen Emeritus for 2026....

item.title: Halloween Carnival in the Park: Sunday, October 25
item.description: Calling all ghouls and goblins! Celebrate Halloween on Sunday, October 25, from 2–4:30pm at Belvedere Community Center and Park. Sponsored by The Ranch, the Halloween Carnival features a reptile show, face painters, balloon twisters, carnival games, pumpkin decorating, and treats! Make sure your parents buy your tickets in advance. Adults accompanying children are free.
